sentences.text: 22.05.2023 Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.332/2016, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Jahangir Puri, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 20:35:43 3.

The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 04.06.2014 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
One child was born out of the said wedlock.
Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and on 04.06.2016, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 28.01.2023 arrived at before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini Courts for taking divorce by mutual consent.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.
On 21.04.2023 petitioner no.1 gave the divorce as per Muslim rites.
5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 20:35:43 served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.332/2016, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC,
registered at Police Station Jahangir Puri, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

However, the rights of the child born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains the majority as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh V. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos.4031-4032 of 2019.
8.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MAY 22, 2023/ib
